<meta>continues from previous page: a monk who has promised to spend the rains at a residence leaves on business that takes up to seven days</meta>
<header>III. 14. 6-11. MAHĀVAGGA. 155</header>

He comes back within that week. For that monk, O monks, the earlier rains-residence is recognized, and there is no offence in respect of his promise. ||6|| Here again . . . he leaves, having business to attend to, when the Pavāraṇā is seven days away. Whether that monk comes back to that residence or does not come back, O monks, for that monk the earlier rains-residence is recognized, and there is no offence in respect of his promise. ||7|| Here again, O monks, a monk has promised to spend the rains for the earlier period. He goes to that residence and holds the Uposatha; on the first day of the fortnight he comes to the dwelling, makes ready his lodging, sets out drinking water and water for washing, and sweeps the cell. On that very day he leaves, having no business to attend to. For that monk, O monks, the earlier rains-residence is not recognized, and in respect of his promise there is an offence of wrong-doing. ||8|| Here again . . . (= § 8) . . . he leaves on that very day, having business to attend to . . . and so on . . . having stayed two or three days, he leaves, having no business to attend to . . . and so on . . . having stayed two or three days, he leaves, having business to attend to . . . and so on . . . having stayed two or three days, he leaves on business that takes up to seven days. He spends that week outside. For that monk, O monks, the earlier rains-residence is not recognized, and in respect of his promise there is an offence of wrong-doing. ||9|| Having stayed two or three days, he leaves on business that takes up to seven days. He comes back within that week. For that monk, O monks, the earlier rains-residence is recognized, and there is no offence in respect of his promise. When seven days . . . (= § 7) . . . no offence. ||10|| Here again, O monks, a monk has promised to spend the rains for the later period. While going to that residence he holds the Uposatha outside; on the first day of the fortnight he comes to the dwelling, makes ready his lodging, sets out drinking water and water for washing, and sweeps the cell. On that very day he leaves, having no business to attend to. For that monk, O monks, the later rains-residence is not recognized, and in respect of his promise there is an offence of wrong-doing. Here again . . . (the whole passage is identical with § 5-10; read "the later" and "for the later period" instead of "the earlier" and "for the earlier period", and instead of "when the Pavāraṇā is seven days away": "when the Komudī full moon of the fourth month is seven days away") . . . there is no offence in respect of his promise. ||11||14||
<note>The <term>vassa</term> <gloss>rains retreat</gloss> could be entered for an earlier period <term>purimikā</term> or a later one <term>pacchimikā</term>, beginning a month apart. <term>Uposatha</term> is the fortnightly observance day; <term>Pavāraṇā</term> is the "invitation" ceremony that closes the earlier rains. <term>Dukkaṭa</term> <gloss>wrong-doing</gloss> is the lightest class of offence in the monastic code. The <term>Komudī</term> is the full moon of the month Kattika, closing the fourth month of the rainy season.</note>

End of the third section, on entering upon the rains.
<note>original: "vassupanâyikakkhandhako tatiyo"</note>

Its summary:
Entering, and when, and how many, and in the midst of the rains,
and they do not wish, and deliberately, to postpone, a lay follower.|
<note>This <term>uddāna</term> <gloss>mnemonic summary</gloss> lists the topics of the section by key words; the verse continues on the next page.</note>

<summary>This page ends the Vinaya's section on entering the rains retreat (Mahāvagga III), setting out when a monk who promised a rains-residence and then leaves is credited with it and when he incurs an offence of wrong-doing. It closes with the section title and the opening of its mnemonic summary verse.</summary>
